_meta.description: Loan ledger impact of transferring the 9 Kyle-billed inventory items in Ty's 2026-11-06 handoff PDF from Kyle's side (M77 Ag loan) to Ty's side (M5 Ag loan). Per Kyle's direction 2026-11-11: 'if kyle bought them, they need to transferred to Ty, so there needs to be a reductions from Kyle's loan and added to Ty's loan.' The transfer is an intercompany ownership adjustment — physical inventory now lives under Ty's M5 Ag account, so the loan ownership moves with it.
_meta.methodology: The 9 items identified as 'ownership mismatch' in ty-inventory-invoice-match.json (Sulfen, Metrybuzin, Status, Peak, Clethodim, Flagstaff, 24D Amine, Hydrovant, Meso) totaling $72,150 were purchased on invoices billed to 'Kyle McConnell / Acre Profit' at Sims, to 'Acre Profit LLC' at Jabco, or to 'ToGo AG LLC' at Corbet. Those purchases were funded by Kyle/M77 Ag/ToGo (Kyle's side). Transferring the inventory to Ty means Kyle's side gets credit; Ty's side takes on the obligation.

correctedBalances.note: Total outstanding unchanged ($463,318.36) — this is an intercompany reallocation. Kyle's loan reduced by $72,150; Ty's loan increased by $72,150. AcreProfit still owes the same total; who it owes it to has shifted.

unitValuedAtKylePurchaseCost.note: If instead of valuing the transfer at Ty's handoff prices, we value it at Kyle's actual Sims/Jabco/Corbet acquisition costs (what Kyle's loan actually originated), the transfer amount is DIFFERENT. Kyle may want to use ACQUISITION COST for the loan transfer (true dollar-for-dollar), not Ty's markup prices.

items.costBasis: Sims 180@$76 + Sims 180@$76 + Jabco 180@$71.50 blended for 330 gal subset
Sims $42/gal (Jabco variant is $45.50 but only Sims reference used)

unitValuedAtKylePurchaseCost.note: At acquisition cost basis: Kyle's loan drops by $65,596 (to $105,023.31); Ty's loan rises by $65,596 (to $358,295.05). Difference between Ty's handoff price ($72,150) and acquisition cost ($65,596) = $6,554 of built-in margin on Ty's PDF — that's trading margin that would accrue to whichever side keeps the inventory.

recommendation: Kyle picks one of two options, confirms with Ty, and we lock in: (A) Transfer at Ty's handoff prices ($72,150) — easier because Ty's PDF numbers stand as-is; (B) Transfer at acquisition cost ($65,596) — fairer because it preserves the actual cash-outlay math and leaves ~$6,554 of implied margin as a separate P&L question. Either way, total outstanding stays at $463,318.36 — the question is just the split between Kyle's M77 Ag loan and Ty's M5 Ag loan.
